newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar and the basket of currencies on Wednesday after the Bank of Israel intervened to support the basket, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today with slightly more conversions of foreign currencies into shekels. The basket (which on Tuesday reached the bottom edge of its trading band) continued to decline and the Bank of Israel had to intervene," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band for four months.
The dealer said the central bank intervened to the tune of $80 million to support the basket.

The basket came under renewed pressure following the decision of the central bank on Monday to hold its key lending rate for June at an annualised 13.9 percent, the level at which it has been since the end of February.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3950 shekels against 3.3940 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6957 shekels against 3.6947 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9279 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9335 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9940 shekels compared with 1.9969 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3945 shekels.
